correctness.rationale: For every n>=1 and alpha>0, exact Pareto truncated moments M_p(t) yield the variance and its three sharp small-t regimes. Tonelli gives the mean threshold; integration gives the rational trace and three boundary poles. For each finite realized sample the empirical min-characteristic function equals t times its sample mean sufficiently close to zero, yielding the almost-sure threshold and three boundary rates. A separable-Hilbert CLT establishes the finite-trace quadratic-Gaussian limit, without claiming an infinite-mean CLT. The standalone checker passes 83 rational and numerical comparisons. The nonzero sample-mean coefficient for alpha>1 holds a.s. by absolute continuity.

value.rationale: Pareto-heavy-tail goodness-of-fit is explicitly motivated in the parent min-characteristic test literature. Increasing spectral mass near zero can separate almost-sure computational finiteness from finite-null-expectation calibration; the precise transition occurs for every shape alpha<2. The trace is exact for every finite sample n, with different pole orders at alpha=2, and the result identifies the regime allowing conventional Gaussian-Hilbert null calibration. These are natural invariant/feasibility properties rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; no unproved power claim is needed.
